scenes.headline: How a text-only model draws the Earth
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cobbler! A language model has never seen a map. Here's how to get one out of it anyway.

scenes.text: Ask a model whether one coordinate is land or water, for every point on a 2° grid, and the answers paint the world it learned from text.
scenes.say: Ask if one coordinate is land or water, at every point of a two degree grid. Side by side, the answers paint the world the model learned from text.

scenes.title: One pixel per prompt
scenes.say: Each pixel is its own prompt.

items.text: Pick a point on the grid
items.say: Pick a point. The grid is ninety rows by one hundred and eighty columns.
Write the coordinate as text, and ask for one word.
Don't parse the reply. Read the scores of the two answer words.
Paint one pixel. Sixteen thousand two hundred prompts later, you have a map.

steps.say: Here's Celeste's chart. An older model says land almost everywhere, and scores below one that just says water.
The newest one, thinking first, draws coastlines, islands and the Antarctic shelf.

scenes.title: Area-weighted accuracy
scenes.note: Read every score against the always-Water floor
scenes.say: Saying water everywhere already scores seventy-one percent. Every score has to beat that floor.

scenes.label: of the best model's wrong points sit on the coastal ring
scenes.note: a ring that holds 22% of the grid
scenes.say: Read the chart back cell by cell. The best model's mistakes sit on the coast, and seventeen are lakes the key calls land.

steps.say: Feed the model a place, as text.
By the middle of the network, that place is a point in the model's activation space.
A probe that is just one matrix reads latitude and longitude back out. A curved probe barely helps.
The eval reads the other way. Land or water is a property of where the coordinate lands. That link is our inference.

scenes.text: The full grid buys the picture, not the score: 648 points already score 99.6%.
scenes.say: Thin the grid to six hundred and forty-eight points and the score barely moves. The full grid buys the coastline.

recap: One prompt, two token scores, one pixel
Coordinates are a straight line inside
scenes.say: One prompt per pixel. Score it against the floor. The map was in there all along.
